answer: I would like to talk about someone whose work I have seen at close quarters for many years. The person is our family doctor, who is genuinely excellent at what he does. He runs a small practice near our home in Sirajganj and has looked after my family since I was a child. Beyond his obvious medical knowledge, what makes him stand out is how he treats patients as people rather than cases. He is incredibly [[thorough]], always taking the time to explain things clearly instead of rushing you out of the door. I have noticed that he has a calming presence, which is [[invaluable]] when you are worried about your health. He also keeps himself up to date, so his advice always feels current and trustworthy. What impresses me most is his [[dedication]]; he clearly sees medicine as a vocation, not just a job. I remember him coming to our flat late one night during the monsoon when my father had a high fever, which he certainly did not have to do. Because of this, the entire community trusts him completely, and appointments are always fully booked. I think being good at a job like his requires both skill and genuine [[empathy]], and he has both in abundance. As for how I feel about him, I have enormous respect for him. Honestly, he has set my expectations of what a good professional should be, and I try to bring some of his patience to my own work.

followUps.q: Would you like to have a job like his?
followUps.answer: Not really. I admire doctors enormously, but I do not think I could cope with the pressure or the sight of blood. I am much happier helping people in a less [[high-stakes]] way.

followUps.q: Do you think doctors are well respected in your country?
followUps.answer: Generally yes, especially good ones like him. Doctors are highly regarded in Bangladesh, and many parents dream of their children becoming one, although the profession is extremely demanding.
